subtype: Approach: writing a to-do list and dividing jobs at home [Action]
passage: Only three days remained, and Chinmay had a pencil, a sheet of paper and a problem. He wrote a list: cake, invitations, decorations, games. Then he called his family to the table. "Mahima didi, can you order the cake with Papa?" "Fine," said his sister. "Mummy, decorations?" "I have old streamers," she said. His little brother took the games. Chinmay kept invitations for himself, because he loved to draw. That evening he drew a rocket on every card, folded each one and wrote a name inside. By the second night nine were done, and only the glue stick was missing. He checked the item off with a smile.

qa.q: Which job did Chinmay keep for himself?
Why did Chinmay keep the invitations for himself?
qa.a: Chinmay loves to draw, so this job suited him and let him enjoy the work.

qa.q: What alternative approach could help if a helper does not finish a job, and why?
qa.a: Chinmay could check in halfway through the three days and swap a job that is behind. Seeing the list often helps everyone notice what is late in time to fix it.

qa.q: How might Mahima see being asked to order the cake?
qa.a: Mahima probably feels trusted and included; being handed a real task means the party is a shared effort and not only Chinmay's.

grounding: A boy lists the cake, invitations, decorations and games and gives family members a job each, keeping the drawn invitations for himself.

subtype: Approach: writing a to-do list and dividing jobs at home [Action]
passage: Pradeep tore a page from his rough book and wrote PARTY in capitals. Under it: cake, invitations, decorations, games. Then he went round their Lucknow flat with the page. Papa agreed to order the cake from the bakery near the market. His elder brother Vijay, groaning, took decorations. "And games?" Pradeep asked. "Dadi," said Mummy. "She knows fifty." That left invitations. Pradeep smiled. He was the best drawer in 5B. He spent Sunday afternoon making twelve cards, each with a different cartoon animal holding a balloon, and ticked 'invitations' off the list himself.

qa.q: What did Pradeep draw on each invitation?
qa.a: A different cartoon animal holding a balloon.

qa.q: How did Pradeep feel when invitations were left for him?
qa.a: He smiled, so he felt pleased and confident, being the best drawer in 5B.

qa.q: What could Pradeep add to his list to keep the jobs on track?
qa.a: A date next to each job and a quick check a few days before; giving each person one job is what spread the work.

qa.q: How does Vijay feel about his job?
qa.a: Vijay groans as he takes decorations, so he seems a bit reluctant, though he still agrees.

grounding: Shows a boy listing party jobs, giving one each to family members, and keeping the invitations for himself because he draws well.

subtype: Approach: writing a to-do list and dividing jobs at home [Action]
passage:
"Ammi, I made a list. Cake, invitations, decorations, games."
"Very organised, Yusuf. Who's doing what?"
"You and Abbu: cake. Can you ask Chandrika Aunty upstairs? She bakes."
"I'll ask her. Next?"
"Samina: decorations. You're good with streamers."
His sister looked up from her phone. "What do I get?"
"My eternal thanks."
"Fine. Streamers."
"Abbu: games. Musical chairs and passing the parcel."
"And you?" Ammi asked.
"Invitations. I'll draw them, each one different." He was already pulling out his sketch pens. "Ten cards. I'll finish them tonight."
Abbu called from the balcony, "Games? I haven't played passing the parcel in thirty years!"

qa.q: Which two games did Yusuf give Abbu?
qa.a: Musical chairs and passing the parcel.

qa.q: How does Yusuf seem to feel about doing the invitations himself?
qa.a: He seems eager and confident, already pulling out his sketch pens and promising ten cards by tonight.

qa.q: What could Yusuf do if one job falls behind?
qa.a: Check the list a few days before and swap jobs if needed; giving each person one clear job is what makes the plan work.

qa.q: How does Abbu see his job?
qa.a: Abbu is amused and a little surprised to be running games after thirty years, but seems happy to join in.

grounding: Illustrates a boy writing a party to-do list, asking family members to take a job each, and making the invitations himself because he draws.
